meta.title: Helpdesk Atlas
meta.subtitle: The same system as the hand-authored plate: prism height is write volume, one instance per deployment

plate.datum: relief: prism height is write volume, about 7 transcript rows per turn

steps.title: CLIENT → CASES SERVICE
steps.story: A staff member types “which warehouse serves this product?”. The page POSTs it with the bearer and keeps one SSE stream open; nothing else in the browser talks to the backend.

steps.title: MESSAGE → SIGNAL
steps.story: The service does signalWithStart on the conversation workflow, id = session id. If the workflow does not exist yet this creates it; if it does, the message is queued in workflow state and never dropped — even while the worker is down, which is the case that wedged the old runtime.

steps.title: TASK → WORKFLOW
steps.story: Temporal hands the worker a task. The workflow appends turn.started and message.received to the transcript and decides: agent mode, so the model may speak.

steps.title: WORKFLOW → MODEL STEP
steps.story: One llmStep activity. The conversation plus the eight tool schemas go to the model with stopWhen stepCountIs(1), so it answers or asks for exactly one tool. Heartbeats on every delta keep Temporal from timing it out.

steps.title: MODEL STEP → OPENROUTER
steps.story: claude-haiku-4.5 over HTTPS, about 3.4k input tokens per step. Caching cannot hit yet: the stable prefix sits under the 4096-token minimum.

steps.title: TOOL CALL
steps.story: The model asked for ecs_relationships. The workflow dispatches a toolCall activity, which runs one plain function behind the read-only guard.

steps.title: GET ONLY → REST-API
steps.story: inventory_position → located_at → warehouse, read from the client’s accepted state on staging. No write can leave this box: the guard throws on anything but GET.

steps.title: EVERY EVENT → TRANSCRIPT
steps.story: action.result, step.completed, message.completed, session.waiting: each is a transcriptWrite activity, idempotent on (session, seq), then streamed live to the page. About seven rows per turn.

steps.title: “ESCALATE” → CASE
steps.story: The escalate tool is special-cased: the workflow startChild’s the support case, flips itself to human, and from then on offers no tools and calls no model. Passivity is state, not a prompt.

steps.title: CASE → TICKET
steps.story: The case writes a ticket file (Asana later) and waits. A wait of days costs nothing: no process holds anything open, the history is the state.

steps.title: SUPPORT REPLIES
steps.story: From the console, “Send as support” is POST /cases/:id/reply, which becomes a humanReplied signal on the case. The text is routed to the conversation as human.message and published over SSE. It never enters the model.

steps.title: HAND BACK → ASSISTANT RESUMES
steps.story: “Hand back to assistant” signals deescalate; the case routes it to its parent; the conversation flips to agent and answers on the same transcript. Escalate again and it is still one case, one ticket.

database.label: Store — a database or a directory

views.label: Ask and answer
views.note: A question becomes a signal. Model activities and read-only tools answer it; transcript events stream back to the browser.

views.label: Escalate
views.note: The escalate tool starts the support case as a child workflow. The assistant goes passive by state: no tools offered, no model called.

views.label: The human
views.note: A support reply is a signal on the case, routed to the conversation and published straight to the browser. It never enters the model.

views.label: What was removed
views.note: Eve and its Postgres world owned the session until 2026-09-14. Neither resumed a mid-turn crash, so Temporal took the conversation.

dossier.does: The page a client’s staff talks to. Airbnb-style support messaging: streamed answers, tool activity in plain words, a case card when a human takes over, the support person as a named bubble.
dossier.built: web/index.html, app.js, app.css served by cases/http.ts on :8787. SSE stream with a per-session seq cursor and gapless reconnect; light/dark; settings drawer; verified in Chrome with Playwright (scripts/ui-check.mjs).

dossier.does: The inbox a support human uses: open cases with status pills, the user’s transcript, reply, hand back, mark resolved.
dossier.built: web/console.html. GET /cases, GET /cases/:id/transcript, POST /cases/:id/{reply,handback,close}; every action becomes a Temporal signal on the case workflow.

dossier.does: The only door into the system. Accepts a message, opens the live stream, exposes case status and the support endpoints, and serves both pages.
dossier.built: POST /sessions/:id/message = signalWithStart(conversationWorkflow, workflowId = sessionId). GET /sessions/:id/stream replays helpdesk_transcript by seq then tails live chunks. Static route for web/.

dossier.does: Holds every workflow’s history. Whatever dies, the system resumes from here: the worker, the HTTP service, Postgres, even this server itself.
dossier.built: Dev: temporal server start-dev --db-filename. It is in-memory by default, so durability tests must pass a file. Prod: self-hosted server + Postgres, or Temporal Cloud.

dossier.does: The event history of every conversation and case. The source of truth for replay.
dossier.built: SQLite file in dev; Postgres or Cassandra behind a self-hosted server in prod.

dossier.does: The conversation itself as a durable state machine: it queues your messages, decides when the model may speak, goes passive while a human holds the case, and resumes on handback.
dossier.built: Signals userMessage / humanReplied / deescalate / close; query status. Each model step, tool call and transcript write is an activity. Passivity is state: while human, no tool is offered and no model is called.

dossier.does: One escalation. Opens a ticket, waits for a human for as long as it takes at zero compute, routes their reply back to the conversation, then hands back or closes.
dossier.built: startChild from the conversation on escalate, ParentClosePolicy ABANDON, workflowId <sessionId>:case. A parentless case is refused (non-retryable). Signals humanRequested / humanReplied / deescalate / close.

dossier.does: Where a case becomes something a team can see. Files today, Asana next.
dossier.built: .spike/tickets/<caseId>.json, idempotent on caseId, behind the TicketSink interface.

dossier.does: One model step: read the conversation, then either answer or ask for a tool.
dossier.built: AI SDK streamText, stopWhen stepCountIs(1), tools declared without execute so the SDK returns tool calls. Heartbeat on every delta; 90s timeout, 3 attempts. Deltas stream to the page and are never persisted.

dossier.does: Reads the client’s data: products, inventory positions, warehouses, documents.
dossier.built: Eight plain functions behind a read-only guard, GET only: find_product, product_facts, ecs_entities, ecs_components, ecs_relationships, read_view, list_documents, describe_api.

dossier.does: Writes every event of every conversation to Postgres, in order. Tall because it fires about seven times per turn.
dossier.built: Idempotent upsert on (session_id, seq); the pool resets after a Postgres blip; retries bounded at about four minutes; then a best-effort stream chunk for live fan-out.

dossier.does: Returns the acknowledgement line with a wait estimate.
dossier.built: Constant today; production would use a rolling median of first-response times.

dossier.does: Pushes a support reply to the browser channel. The human never passes through the model.
dossier.built: POST /cases/:id/publish → JSONL + SSE fan-out, deduped by seq.

dossier.does: Every event of every conversation, in order. What the page replays on reload.
dossier.built: Postgres 16, PRIMARY KEY (session_id, seq), created under an advisory lock so the worker and the HTTP service do not race.
@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider, anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5. Prompt caching needs cache_control and a prompt over 4096 tokens; today it is ~3.5k, so it does not hit.
velosport staging over TLS, one bearer per deployment, no tenant model yet ([[cod-7hdsz36x]]). Next: WorkOS scopes, so the agent can also read the ops telemetry it needs to debug a broken system.

dossier.does: Used to own the session here. Removed after its self-hosted durability failed to resume mid-turn crashes on both of its worlds.
dossier.built: Postgres world: the Graphile Worker lock is reclaimed only after four hours. Local world: killed runs stayed running forever, even under a built eve start. Measured three ways; see REPORT.md and ADR [[whs-4hpbq3iw]].

dossier.does: Eve’s Postgres world. The data was durable, but a four-hour lock lease turned any crash into a stranded conversation.
dossier.built: @workflow/world-postgres 5.0.0-beta on Graphile Worker; is_available has no age term and the four hours live in resetLockedAt, not in config.
